test_cases.title: Valid credential login returns success response with no row duplication
test_cases.given: a fixture user with a valid password_hash and must_reset_password=false
test_cases.when: the user POSTs the correct email/password to /api/auth/login
test_cases.then: the response is 200 with a LoginResponse body containing token, and the users table row count is unchanged (no insert, no duplicate)

test_cases.title: Login response never exposes password_hash or must_reset_password
test_cases.given: a fixture user with a valid credential
test_cases.then: the response body contains only the LoginResponse fields (token) and never includes password_hash or must_reset_password

test_cases.title: Login with non-existent email returns generic 401
test_cases.given: an email with no matching user record in the fixture set
test_cases.when: the client POSTs that email with any password to /api/auth/login
test_cases.then: the response is 401 with body "Invalid email or password."

test_cases.title: Login with wrong password returns byte-for-byte identical response to unknown-email case
test_cases.given: a fixture user with a valid credential and the wrong password supplied
test_cases.when: the client POSTs the valid email with an incorrect password to /api/auth/login
test_cases.then: the response status and body are byte-for-byte identical to AUTH-02-TC-03's response, with no field-specific validation error distinguishing the two cases

test_cases.title: Login rejected for user with must_reset_password=true using the same generic error
test_cases.given: a fixture user whose must_reset_password flag is true
test_cases.when: the user attempts to log in with any password
test_cases.then: the response is byte-for-byte identical to the generic 401 in AUTH-02-TC-03/04, and no authentication succeeds

test_cases.title: Startup migration provisions every credential-less row with a random unusable hash
test_cases.given: a fixture set of rows, some with password_hash set and some with password_hash null
test_cases.then: every previously-null row now has a non-null password_hash (unique per row, never a fixed string) and must_reset_password=true, while previously-hashed rows are untouched

test_cases.title: Re-running the provisioning migration is a no-op for already-provisioned rows
test_cases.given: a users table where the migration has already run once
test_cases.then: no rows are updated (password_hash values and must_reset_password flags are unchanged from the first run)

test_cases.title: Provisioning script sets a real password and clears must_reset_password
test_cases.given: a fixture user with must_reset_password=true and an operator-supplied plaintext password
test_cases.when: set_user_initial_password is invoked with the user's email and the plaintext password
test_cases.then: the user's password_hash changes to a value that verifies against the supplied password via verify_credentials, must_reset_password becomes false, and the user can subsequently log in per AUTH-02-TC-01

test_cases.title: Provisioning script never logs or persists the plaintext password
test_cases.given: an operator invokes the set_initial_password script with a plaintext password via captured stdin
test_cases.when: the script completes successfully or fails (user not found)
test_cases.then: the plaintext password never appears in captured logs, stdout/stderr, or any persisted field other than as the input to the hash function, and the script exits 0 on success / 1 on failure

test_cases.title: Login rate limiter returns 429 after 3 failed attempts per email within 60 minutes
test_cases.given: 3 failed login attempts have already been made for the same email within the last 60 minutes
test_cases.when: a 4th login attempt is made for that email within the same rolling window
test_cases.then: the response is 429 with a Retry-After header, regardless of whether the 4th attempt's credentials would otherwise be valid

test_cases.title: Auth logic is isolated in AuthService, not added to UserService
test_cases.given: the backend/app/services module tree after implementation
test_cases.when: app.services.auth_service and app.services.user_service are imported and introspected
test_cases.then: login, provision_existing_users_with_random_password, and set_user_initial_password exist only on AuthService, and UserService exposes no auth-related methods

test_cases.title: Login endpoint meets p95 latency budget under sustained load
test_cases.given: the login endpoint under a sustained load of 50 RPS for 60 seconds
test_cases.when: requests are issued against /api/auth/login with a mix of valid and invalid credentials
test_cases.then: p95 response latency is under 400ms for the full 60-second window

budget.measured: assertion passed (p95 < 0.400s); harness (tests/perf/test_login_perf.py) does not print the raw p95 value, only asserts the bound

test_cases.title: Failed and successful login attempts are logged with opaque keys only, never plaintext email or password
test_cases.given: a mix of successful and failed login attempts, including one for a non-existent email
test_cases.when: logs are captured for the duration of the test
test_cases.then: no log line contains a plaintext email address or password; all authentication log entries reference only user_id or a hashed email
